affected_system: food access, environmental health inspection, and community protection
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of environmental-health inspection and food-support resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for environmental-health inspection and food-support resources
pair risk-tiered minimum-access resource allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Food outlets, inspections, assistance, prices, access, and environmental complaints have separate semantics.
Area food access is not treated as individual diet, food security, or health outcome.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for environmental-health inspection and food-support resources.

constraints.description: The food access and environmental health allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: environmental health commissioner and food-access program director
decision_question: How should inspectors, sampling, emergency food, refrigeration, and navigation capacity be distributed?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The food access and environmental health allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for environmental-health inspection and food-support resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority cases and eligible demand without assigned capacity

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting environmental-health inspection and food-support resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority cases and eligible demand without assigned capacity
distributional gap in priority cases and eligible demand without assigned capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned inspections, benefits, or food supplies as completed or received.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for environmental-health inspection and food-support resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate inspectors, food support, and field resources
transportability_risks: Retail markets, informal food systems, inspection law, mobility, prices, and eligibility vary.
Administrative participation can understate eligible need.
